hook: David Holz built the generative image tool that made AI art a mainstream habit. Before Midjourney, he spent more than a decade as co-founder and CTO of Leap Motion, developing hand-tracking hardware that never found its mass market. He founded Midjourney in 2021 as an independent research lab, kept it privately held, and grew it past 20 million users without taking outside investment. He describes the project as an attempt to expand human imagination rather than to build imaginative machines, and Disney and Universal's 2025 copyright lawsuit against the company shows how far that project now reaches into the rest of the entertainment industry.

standing.record: The site's records center on Midjourney, a San Francisco startup founded in 2021, with no funding or valuation recorded. They also carry Holz's earlier company, Leap Motion, which he co-founded in 2008 and where he served as CTO until its 2019 acquisition by Ultrahaptics. His background includes applied mathematics at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, a departure from his PhD program to build Leap Motion, contracted work for NASA's Langley Research Center, and research at the Max Planck Institute. The legal record lists EVOX Production LLC v. Midjourney, Warner Bros. Entertainment Inc. v. Midjourney, and Disney Enterprises, Inc. and Universal v. Midjourney, all involving the company he founded. It also lists Andersen v. Stability AI Ltd., active and heading toward the first U.S. AI copyright jury trial, though the supplied records do not name Holz or Midjourney in that case. The pattern is a privately held AI image company facing multiple copyright suits from entertainment and production entities while its founder's public profile is recognized by TIME and the Society for Science.
standing.standing: David Holz stands as the founder of Midjourney, the generative image company he launched in August 2021 as an independent research lab. The records show Midjourney is privately held, has grown past 20 million users, and has taken no outside investment. He describes the project as an attempt to expand human imagination rather than to build imaginative machines. His current influence is also recorded through his 2025 naming to TIME's TIME100 AI list and his 2026 naming to the Society for Science's Board of Trustees. The Disney and Universal 2025 copyright lawsuit against Midjourney shows that his company now reaches into the entertainment industry. Before Midjourney, he co-founded Leap Motion in 2008 and served as its CTO until it was acquired by Ultrahaptics in 2019.
